stories.title: Sierra and Meta Unveil Personal Agent Protocol — Walmart, Shopify, Stripe Named as Partners
stories.body: On October 6, 2026, Sierra and Meta announced the Personal Agent Protocol (PAP), an OAuth-based open standard defining how consumers' personal AI agents authenticate and interact with enterprise systems via websites, APIs, or a company's own agent. Partners named at launch include Walmart, Shopify, Stripe, Genesys, Rocket, and Instinct; Meta's list also adds NiCE and Decagon. Sierra published a Draft 0.1 on October 9 and named 35 additional design partners including OpenAI, with a reference implementation and design workshops to follow later in October.
stories.why: PAP directly changes the enterprise architecture conversation: retailers must now decide whether to expose their product catalog, inventory, and order APIs to incoming personal agents or risk being skipped entirely — Meta's own post stated 'turning away a personal agent means turning away the customer behind it.' For a Graas seller, this is proof that the context layer (governed SKU data, live inventory, policy rules) is no longer optional back-office plumbing — it becomes the handshake point every inbound agent will hit first.

stories.tag: US - analyst research / why pilots stall
stories.title: Gartner: 40% of Agentic AI Projects Will Be Canceled by 2027 — Costs, Unclear ROI, and Governance Are the Killers
stories.body: Gartner's widely-cited forecast predicts more than 40% of enterprise agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027, with analyst Anushree Verma identifying three root causes: escalating costs, unclear business value, and inadequate risk controls — not model failure. Separately, Gartner also warns that 40% of companies will need to roll back or disable already-live autonomous agents by 2027 after governance gaps surface in production incidents. McKinsey's August 2026 State of AI survey reinforces the picture: only about 20% of organizations have scaled agents in any function, and 80% of firms using AI see no P&L impact at all.
stories.why: This is the exact objection retail CIOs raise in the second meeting — 'we tried a pilot and it went nowhere.' Gartner names the three failure drivers (cost, value definition, governance) that a governed context layer directly addresses by giving agents a trustworthy, auditable data foundation before they touch production workflows. Sellers can use this to reframe Graas not as another pilot but as the prerequisite infrastructure that makes the 60% of projects that do survive stick.

stories.title: Uvi Launches Knowledge Graph Platform to Stop Enterprises Paying Frontier Models to Re-Learn Their Own Business
stories.body: Israeli startup Uvi, covered by Blocks & Files on October 12, 2026, argues that every AI agent an enterprise deploys starts with zero institutional knowledge and must reconstruct that context from scratch — with the enterprise paying a frontier model each time it does. Uvi's platform uses knowledge graph technology to surface the hidden enterprise context that existing systems hold but cannot expose, so agents can act on it without repeated re-grounding costs. The company positions its offering directly against the pattern of per-query frontier model spend that compounds as agent deployments scale.
stories.why: Uvi names exactly the architecture gap Graas fills: agents that lack a governed context layer burn token budget re-learning what the enterprise already knows, making agentic AI economically unsustainable at scale. On a sales call, this is a concrete cost-of-inaction argument — the longer a retailer waits to build a context layer, the more they pay frontier models to rediscover their own SKU logic, pricing rules, and customer identity.

stories.title: Sierra Raises $950M at $15.8B; Salesforce Acquires Fin for ~$3.6B — Agent Vendor Consolidation Accelerates
stories.body: Sierra raised $950 million in a May 2026 Series E led by Tiger Global and GV at a $15.8 billion post-money valuation, with CEO Bret Taylor telling CNBC that Sierra now serves more than 40% of the Fortune 50. Salesforce agreed to acquire Intercom's Fin agent for approximately $3.6 billion in June 2026, the first major exit check on what an AI customer-service business is actually worth outside a funding round. Decagon, the closest pure-play rival, had tripled its own valuation to $4.5 billion in January 2026 after a $250 million Series D, but now faces a competitor with three times its funding and a CRM bundle threat from Salesforce-Fin.
stories.why: Retailers evaluating agent vendors are walking into a market where the top two or three platforms are pulling away fast on capital and Fortune 50 logos — price leverage and negotiating room for buyers will shrink quickly. For Graas sellers, the consolidation argument is that vendor-specific agent platforms (Sierra, Fin/Salesforce, Decagon) each own their own context store, creating lock-in risk; a vendor-neutral context layer lets the retailer switch or run multiple agent runtimes without rebuilding their data foundation each time.

stories.title: BCG: Agentic Supply Chain Platform Delivers +2–4% In-Stock Lift and 40–60% Admin Savings for CPG Client
stories.body: BCG's May 2026 Executive Perspectives report on AI in supply chains documents a CPG company that deployed a multi-subagent planning platform covering inventory replenishment, order optimization, and S&OP allocation — with human analysts retaining final decision authority during the pilot phase. Measured outcomes include a 2–4 percentage point improvement in in-stock rate (driving direct revenue lift), a 4–10% fill-rate improvement, and 40–60% administrative time savings. BCG's framing is that the pilot is explicitly designed as a template for an organization-wide model shift, with agents taking progressively more direct system actions as trust is established.
stories.why: This is a named-outcome proof point in the exact workflow category — replenishment and ordering — where Graas agents operate, and BCG's human-in-the-loop architecture mirrors the staged deployment model retailers need to hear about to get budget approved. Sellers can use the 40–60% admin savings figure and the in-stock lift to anchor ROI conversations with supply chain and merchandising leaders who need P&L-linked numbers before they escalate to the CIO.
